a.label: Detection and High Resolution Tracking of Vehicles at Hypersonic Velocities

edges.label: subject domain: sensing and tracking at hypersonic velocity
edges.note: The sensor-side counterpart to Leonhardt's cloaking DIRD: one asks how an object could be made undetectable, the other how an object moving at hypersonic velocity could nevertheless be tracked at high resolution. Together they bracket the observability problem that any UAP sensor programme has to solve.

edges.note: The DIA list of 9 January 2018 records 'Detection and High Resolution Tracking of Vehicles at Hypersonic Velocities, Dr W Culbreth, Univ of Nevada-Las Vegas.' The released PDF's author block is redacted under (b)(6). Culbreth also wrote 'Aneutronic Fusion Propulsion II'. He is among the few DIRD authors to have discussed the work publicly, in a 2019 interview with George Knapp.

edges.label: commissioned subject-matter author
edges.note: Credited with two of the 38 AAWSAP deliverables: 'Aneutronic Fusion Propulsion II' (1 November 2010) and 'Detection and High Resolution Tracking of Vehicles at Hypersonic Velocities' (20 November 2010, DIA-08-1012-001). Both released texts name AAWSAP. Culbreth was based at the University of Nevada, Las Vegas, the same city as the prime contractor BAASS. b.label: Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies (BAASS), LLC

edges.label: UNLV academic in the prime contractor's home city
edges.note: TIER 3, INFERENTIAL. AAWSAP was executed by BAASS out of southern Nevada, and BAASS subcontracted subject-matter experts to write the DIRDs. Culbreth was the University of Nevada, Las Vegas faculty member credited with two of them. No document in the public record states that BAASS specifically recruited him, and this edge should not be read as one. Both DIRDs cited here have their author field redacted under FOIA exemption (b)(6), so even the crediting rests on DIA's separate list of deliverables rather than on the documents themselves.
